title: Staged opt-in + synthetic canary for RBAC v2 permission mapping and SAML assertion harmonization
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Enable a safe, staged opt-in path for customers to migrate to RBAC v2 by running synthetic canaries and validating SAML/SSO assertion compatibility. This ticket wires together the opt-in UI flag, the synthetic traffic generator, the dual-write reconciliation monitor, and a harmonization test suite for SAML attributes to ensure parity with RBAC v1 before mass cutover.
objective: Provide an automated, reversible migration path that allows customers to opt into RBAC v2 with minimal service disruption and verified permission equivalence, backed by end-to-end telemetry and audit logs for post-migration assurance.
scope:
- Build customer opt-in toggle in Console and API (opt_in=true/false)
- Implement synthetic-canary runner that replays representative auth flows for 50 sample orgs
- Create SAML assertion harmonizer tests to validate NameID, roles, and custom attributes mapping
- Wire dual-write hooks so both RBAC v1 and RBAC v2 receive writes and produce reconciliation diffs
- Add reconciliation dashboard and alerting with remediation runbook links
- Produce customer-facing migration guidance and automated comms templates
out_of_scope:
- Full production cutover for all customers
- Bulk backfill of historical audit events into the new ledger (handled in separate backfill task)
- Changes to SSO provider integrations beyond assertion schema validation
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes an opt-in flag that toggles request routing to RBAC v2 for a single org
Synthetic canary run produces permission equivalence >= 99.5% for sample orgs across read/write operations
SAML harmonization suite verifies mapping for NameID, roles, and three custom attributes for supported IdPs
Dual-write reconciliation job runs every 10 minutes and shows no unreconciled deltas after a 48h warm period for canary orgs
Audit logs include both v1 and v2 entries with identical request IDs and correlation tokens for traceability
Rollback path disables opt-in and routes traffic back to v1 within 30s without permission leakage
tasks: Console: add 'RBAC v2 opt-in' cohort flag and admin consent flow (UX wireframes in linked doc)
API: add org-level boolean opt_in field and admin-only endpoint to toggle
Runtime: implement per-request routing gate that reads opt_in and routes to v2 runtime
Synthetic Canary: implement generator and corpus derived from top 200 API patterns; add seeded org dataset
SAML Tests: build assertion parser and mapping validator; include test vectors for OKTA, AzureAD, OneLogin
Dual-write: implement write fanout to both stores with idempotency keys and tombstone markers
Reconciliation: build job to compute permission diffs, classify delta types (missing, stale, divergent), and surface top 10 causes
Observability: add tracing correlation IDs across proxy, runtime, and ledger; create dashboard and SLO checks
Docs/Comms: draft migration guide, canary signup email, and post-canary FAQ
Security Review: submit artifact for security checklist and SAML assertion threat modeling
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal canary (team orgs) -> Phase 2: 50 seeded customer opt-ins with synthetic canaries -> Phase 3: Gradual cohort expansion by org-size buckets (small -> medium -> large) with 24h observation windows and automated health checks. Each expansion step requires reconciliation delta <0.5% and no critical SLO regressions.
rollback_plan: Immediate opt-in toggle off for cohort; a cleanup job will replay idempotent tombstone updates to v1 store if necessary. Customer-visible effect: new RBAC v2 permissions stop being served; existing v1 permissions remain authoritative. Post-rollback checklist includes audit log correlation, customer notice, and investigation playbook.
observability_checks: Per-org permission delta rate (alerts when > 0.5% of permission checks diverge)
Error rate on SAML assertions parsing (alerts when > 0.1% of assertions fail)
End-to-end latency P95 for auth checks (must not regress beyond 10% of baseline)
Correlation ID absence metric for cross-store tracing (must be < 0.01%)
Reconciliation job success metric and time-to-converge median
testing_plan: Unit tests for assertion parser and mapping logic
Integration tests: full request path with dual-write enabled and replay verification
Synthetic canary runs: nightly and on-demand; store output as artifacts
Chaos test: simulate intermittent write failures and verify idempotent retry logic
Security fuzzing for SAML attributes and role name edge-cases
decisions: Use idempotency-keyed dual-write rather than write-then-forward to reduce race windows
Start with opt-in cohorts; do not expose auto-opt by default to avoid unexpected permission drift
Correlation IDs will be propagated via X-Request-ID and X-RBAC-Correlation headers and logged in both stores
SAML harmonization will attempt benign normalizations (trim, case-normalize) but will not invent roles — divergences will be surfaced to admins for mapping approval
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Divergent permission semantics between v1 and v2 leading to unauthorized denial. Mitigation: fail-open on read-time checks during canary only if reconciliation shows transient staleness and alert owners.
Risk: SAML assertion variance across IdPs. Mitigation: maintain a registry of IdP-specific normalizers and expand test vectors based on customer reportbacks.
Risk: Increased write amplification and storage cost due to dual-write. Mitigation: enable dual-write only for opted-in orgs and prune tombstones after 90 days post-cutover.
Risk: Customer confusion about audit entries. Mitigation: add audit log annotations indicating migration cohort and correlation IDs; publish migration FAQ
updates: 2025-03-03: Kickoff meeting held with PM, Design, Infra. UX wireframes uploaded to linked Confluence page. (Ava)
2025-03-05: Prototype of opt-in API implemented in feature branch github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/compare/opt-in-canary (Jonah)

2025-03-07: First synthetic canary run against internal staging orgs showed 98.2% equivalence; identified 3 normalization edge-cases for role names (whitespace, unicode NFKC, trailing dots). Added normalizer ticket.
2025-03-09: Dual-write fanout implemented; observed transient 200ms median extra write latency. Decided to gate dual-write behind opt-in and perf SLOs. (Design review accepted)
2025-03-10: Security review submitted; requested threat model addendum for SAML assertion replay attack surface. (Security)
Next steps: expand canary corpus to 50 customer-shaped orgs, finalize reconciliation dashboard, run full SAML vector suite against OKTA and AzureAD
notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: the opt-in approach allows customers to self-select into RBAC v2 and provides both us and the customer with audit artifacts to prove equivalence. Keep communication templates simple and emphasize ability to rollback quickly. Coordinate with support and solutions engineering before inviting external customers to canary.
